headline: High: Haystack’s broad network/MCP defaults can leak ComfyUI outputs and create cascading errors; prompt-injection risk is lower because ComfyUI is offline-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline-only and has no clipboard/MCP surface, so it cannot directly ingest Haystack output by default. Haystack can use MCP servers, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or direct parser bridge. The main pathway is manual copy/paste or an added integration, so the risk is limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Haystack text into a ComfyUI workflow prompt or node field, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared MCP or file bridge is added between the agents, Haystack output can influence ComfyUI instructions.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces with no shared clipboard or file mount.
Disable any MCP bridge between Haystack and ComfyUI.
Require manual review before pasting Haystack output into ComfyUI.
Use a fixed prompt template in ComfyUI that ignores free-form instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for any imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model files, while Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints. Even without a shared filesystem, any workflow that passes ComfyUI artifacts into Haystack can expose sensitive media or embeddings to a networked retrieval stack. The pair is not proven to share data by default, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are uploaded into Haystack indexes or prompts, those artifacts can leave the local environment.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or API-backed storage, Haystack may transmit ComfyUI files off-host.
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs in a local-only directory.
Do not index images, seeds, or model artifacts in Haystack unless redacted.
Restrict Haystack connectors to approved internal endpoints.
Review outbound requests from Haystack before enabling production use.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on media and embedding uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, so it has little direct write conflict with Haystack. Haystack can use MCP and broad network egress, but the profiles do not show overlapping mutable local resources or shared locks. Any conflict would require an added shared backend or workspace not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external database or API-backed store, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator maps Haystack actions onto ComfyUI-managed files, resource contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources owned by only one agent.
Avoid shared git or database writes between the agents.
Use separate service accounts for any shared backend.
Add a simple lock or queue around shared writes.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency checks on shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent that can consume upstream content, and ComfyUI can generate workflows, images, and embeddings that Haystack may treat as authoritative inputs. Because Haystack also has REST/MCP action surfaces, a bad ComfyUI output can cascade into downstream retrieval or tool calls unless explicitly verified. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Haystack ingests ComfyUI-generated text, metadata, or captions without validation, errors can propagate.
IF Haystack is configured to act on retrieved content via REST or MCP, a bad upstream artifact can trigger downstream actions.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before Haystack acts on ComfyUI output.
Validate schemas for any ComfyUI-derived metadata.
Separate generation and action pipelines.
Log and sample-check retrieved artifacts for anomalies.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is documented as fully offline and only touches local media/model artifacts, while Haystack’s profile only mentions anonymous usage statistics and broad networked APIs. No specific residency, HIPAA, or GDPR mismatch is documented for either agent, so compliance risk is limited to gaps if operators route regulated data through Haystack.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Haystack connectors or prompts, external processing may create a policy mismatch.
IF ComfyUI outputs contain personal data and are forwarded to Haystack, retention rules may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Haystack by default.
Use local-only ComfyUI workflows for sensitive media.
Document retention settings for any Haystack deployment.
Review vendor terms before enabling external connectors.
requires-engineering: add data-class routing controls.
